current.text: He picked up his 5 million USD player option and is back with Milwaukee.
Experts read the opt-in as a sign that no other team wanted him.
He looks healthy and played in the preseason.
Milwaukee's backcourt is crowded. Rollins, Herro, Burries, Jakucionis, Trent, Green and Watanabe all compete with him for guard minutes.
The projected starters to open the season are Rollins, Herro, Jaquez, Kuzma and Turner, so Porter is not in the projected starting lineup.
Experts expect him to come off the bench as the sixth man and lead the second unit, but they are not sure. A bench role could mean about 27 minutes.
Doc Rivers is no longer the coach, and Porter was his preferred guard. Taylor Jenkins is the new head coach and might use a deep rotation.
Lloyd expects his minutes to be well below last season's under the new coach. Josh thinks he may be pushed down the rotation and is not fully in the team's plans.
Experts do not expect last season's 2.2 steals, 7.4 assists and 88% free throws to repeat. Of last season's steals leaders, he is the most likely to drop a lot.
Experts call him a worthwhile late flyer around picks 110 to 120 and say he should not go before 120. If he reaches 29 minutes, he has top 50 upside.
Experts say the roster needs trades to consolidate. Porter, Kuzma, Jaquez and Herro are named as players who do not fit well.
Milwaukee is expected to put more focus on developing young players as the season goes on, which would cut veteran minutes.

durable.text: He had several knee problems last season and likely more than one surgery.
He scores with tough mid-range shots and takes few threes. Experts think that efficiency is unlikely to last.
He makes few threes for a guard.
Steals are his best category and a real outlier, even in the lower projections.
His FT% is hard to predict. He has a 60% FT season in his career.
Experts call him an inefficient, ball-dominant real-life player, but say his fantasy numbers can be strong.

note: He is priced as a last-round flyer: 3 USD on Yahoo, 2 USD on ESPN and 3 USD in our auction last season. His ranks of 128 and 109 put him near the end of our 144-player pool. That fits the expert consensus of a 1 to 3 USD pick for steals, assists and FT%, best on a punt 3PM build. Early in the season, check whether he gets 29 or more minutes or a starting job, and whether his steals and FT% hold up. If he ends up as a 27-minute bench guard, he is easy to cut.
